subject: [D-RUG]: Add legend using ggplot when data cannot be grouped

messages.author: bb5d7dcfd24b99b9
messages.subject: [D-RUG]: Add legend using ggplot when data cannot be grouped
parts:
Hi all,

First time calling on the D-RUG hivemind so hopefully I did it right...

I am trying to replicate the following plot using ggplot (sans black border around the image and with different data)



Here is what I have so far:


However, I am struggling with adding the legend! It looks like for ggplot, the legend is added when your data can be divided into categorical groups, but I do not have that (I think?). Here is what my data looks like (data frame is called intercept):



And my code:

ggplot(intercept, aes(Day,DSR)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.25) +
  geom_line(aes(day, Lower), linetype = 'dashed', size = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(day, Upper), linetype = 'dashed', size = 1) +
  labs(x ="Age of Nest (days)", y ="Cumulative Survival Probability (25-d)") +
  ggtitle("Daily Survival Rate", subtitle = "97.24%") +
  theme_classic()+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust=0.5, size=16),
        plot.subtitle =element_text(hjust=0.5, size=13),
        axis.line = element_line(size = 1),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size=15),
        axis.text.x = element_text(face="bold", color="black", size=11),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face="bold", color="black", size=11),
        axis.ticks = element_line(size=1))+
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0.4, 1.0), breaks = seq(0.4, 1.0, by =0.1), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,25),expand = c(0,0))

I have scoured the Google, but nothing seems to be working out...or I am implementing the solutions incorrectly.

Anyone have insights?

Sincerely,
Diana A. Muñoz 
(she/her)
Graduate Group in Ecology
University of California, Davis

messages.author: f14d4c9d01f43388
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Add legend using ggplot when data cannot be grouped
parts:
Hi

This is happening because you are manually adding lines, instead of "mapping a variable to an easthetic", in ggplot2 language. A more standard way in ggplot2 would be to turn your data-frame into long, where a new variable would indicate the type (estimate versus CI), then you would have geom_line(linetype = variable).

Without a reproducible example from your data, look at this artificial example:

library(tidyverse)
library(broom)

tidy(lm(freeny), conf.int=TRUE) %>%
  mutate(term = 1:n()) %>%
  select(term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high) %>%
  gather(variable, value, -term) %>% 
  mutate(type = if_else(str_detect(variable, "estimate"), "estimate", "CI") %>% factor(levels = c("estimate", "CI"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=term, y=value, group=variable, linetype=type))+
  geom_line()

messages.author: 91fcdff1323a6831
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Add legend using ggplot when data cannot be grouped
parts:
Hi Diana,
Good question. This is a common one, and as always there are a few approaches. As Matthieu showed, you can make your data "long" and more easily assign a variable to a given aesthetic (i.e., linetype, color, fill, etc).

Alternatively, you can use a scale_.._manual option, and assign something specifically to each geom you are interested in using. I've created a fake dataset so you can run this code, in the future, try to attach the data as a txt file or csv if you want folks to try and recreate your specific plot. Or simulate some data (see below for an example). Hope this helps!

Adios,
Ryan

# Load required libraries
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)

# Make Some Data
dsr <-  exp(seq(0.98, 0.4, length.out = 25))
Day <- seq(1:25)
lower <-  exp(seq(0.975, 0.38, length.out = 25))
upper <-  exp(seq(0.985, 0.42, length.out = 25))
df <- tibble(Day, dsr, upper, lower)

# Make a plot and assign specific items for the legend inside the aes(), you can rename as you like
ggplot() + 
  geom_line(data=df, aes(x=Day, y=dsr, linetype="Estimate"), size = 1.25) +
  geom_line(data=df, aes(x=Day, y=lower, linetype = "CI"), size = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data=df, aes(x=Day, y=upper, linetype = "CI"), size = 0.8) +
labs(x ="Age of Nest (days)", y ="Cumulative Survival Probability (25-d)") +
scale_linetype_manual(name="", values=c("Estimate"=1, "CI"=3))+

ggtitle("Daily Survival Rate", subtitle = "97.24%") +
  theme_classic()+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust=0.5, size=16),
        plot.subtitle =element_text(hjust=0.5, size=13),
        axis.line = element_line(size = 1),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size=15),
        axis.text.x = element_text(face="bold", color="black", size=11),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face="bold", color="black", size=11),
        axis.ticks = element_line(size=1))+

# changed scales slightly to match data
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(1.2, 3.0), breaks = seq(1.2, 3.0, by =0.2), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,25),expand = c(0,0))
